signals.evidence: 11,000 residents of Kiryat Shmona requested a four-night break from alerts and shelters; more than half remained behind due to budget shortage. 6,000+ requests from city residents were rejected.

Esti received physiotherapy, occupational therapy, and psychological support. She states: 'The emotional treatment gave me confidence and the desire to strengthen myself. It helped me greatly with self-image, helped me feel useful, that I can still do things for my children, for my family and for myself.'

Emek Medical Center built and trained significant protected infrastructure in the last three years, including underground protected complexes housing ~300 hospital beds and 10 operating rooms, allowing the hospital to function flexibly and efficiently even under fire and continue providing full medical services to over one million residents.

The Chief Rabbinate issued an exceptional ruling allowing couples forced to postpone weddings due to security directives or reserve service to marry during Sefirat HaOmer (Omer counting period) through the beginning of Iyar, as a temporary measure for this year only.

Minister Miri Regev stated: 'Our goal is to broadcast the ceremony live for the glory of the state. But we are also preparing for a filmed ceremony in case the ceasefire does not hold and we have other security events.' The state is pre-recording the torch-lighting ceremony as a contingency.

Ministry of Education announced a framework of easements in matriculation exams divided by three regions: the front line, the Gulf area and southern Golan, and the rest of the country, including options for internal exams instead of external exams in humanities subjects.

Amit Sofer, head of Mrom HaGalil regional council, said: 'Residents of the front line want real security, not industrial quiet. Even though sleeping several nights in a row is very tempting, we are asking the Israeli government to continue striking Hezbollah until its disarmament.'

Kfar Vardim council informed residents: 'Hezbollah may increase fire in the coming hours. It is recommended to stay near protected spaces and be attentive to Home Front Command instructions. All activities will be stopped.' Maaleh Yosef reported: 'Despite no formal order from Northern Command, there is increased likelihood of rocket fire in the coming hours.'

Residents of the north received the ceasefire announcement with shock. Moshe Davidovitch, head of Mateh Asher regional council, said: 'Agreements are signed in a tie in Washington, but the price is paid in blood, in destroyed homes and in fragmented communities here. A ceasefire announcement without lethal enforcement against Hezbollah violations is not a political achievement, it is a death sentence waiting for the next massacre.'

National Parents' Leadership stated that the matriculation easement framework 'does not provide a real answer to the central need of students—reducing burden and pressure as promised.' Oren Ozen, chair of the national parents' leadership, said: 'These are only point measures that do not reduce the burden in practice and do not change the daily reality in schools.'

Residents of Kiryat Shmona expressed frustration with the ceasefire announcement. Liraz Chernayev said: 'I have a strong sense of déjà vu. Again they are stopping the fighting at its peak. In 2024 they told us Hezbollah was weakened and had no commanders, but after a year and a half rockets and drones flew at us again.' Shlomo Suysa said: 'A new prime minister is imposed on us in the name of Trump—and on northern residents a death sentence is imposed. I feel deceived and frustrated.' Moshe Kakon said: 'This is a cynical move of surrender to Iranian demands.'

Memorial Day ceremonies will be pre-recorded and broadcast if live events cannot be held due to security conditions. The decision on real-time ceremonies will be made close to Memorial Day according to Home Front Command guidance.

Rabbi Doron Peretz, father of Daniel, said: 'Daniel was buried twice. At first we buried his shirt with blood. It was the only grave without a body. Now when I come there, he is there. His body was buried. On one hand, thank God he is not a hostage anymore, but now it is the reality of bereavement. Even though this is the third Memorial Day, it is the first one where Daniel is really there.' Shay, father of Tomer, described: 'For us, the circle did not close when we buried Tomer. Until they returned his brothers we did not mourn as we wanted. Now that everyone is buried, this is the hardest year. It is a seal that drags the loss. It did not become easier, it became harder.'

M., age 43, a manager at an advertising company, struggles to return to work after a month and a half of war. She finds herself unable to lead campaigns that were frozen. Y., age 36, sits in despair. His leg does not stop moving nervously, and he describes sleep difficulties, loss of appetite and low mood that began precisely with the ceasefire announcement.

A resident describes losing self-worth during the war: 'Somewhere between the second and third week of the war I lost my self-respect, and only one word appeared again and again: nothing. I am nothing. I have nothing.' She describes a sharp and sudden fall, like a sugar crash, from feeling all-powerful and vital to becoming an empty shell, drained of all desire.

Less than two hours before the ceasefire took effect at midnight, Hezbollah fired barrages at northern settlements. Medical services reported a man and a girl severely wounded in Carmiel (ages 25 and 17). In Nahariya, a man around 40 was moderately wounded by shrapnel. Two vehicles caught fire in the city. Five people were treated for shock and evacuated to Nahariya hospital.

Alon, mother of Tomer Keren who fell in combat, said: 'Two months before his enlistment he wanted to contribute, and with friends from the Scouts he collected donations for soldiers and northern residents. In the current war I continue his path in the 'Tomer's Roar' initiative. We do what Tomer did: stand in supermarkets with volunteers from the Scouts, ask shoppers to donate supplies and transport them to soldiers fighting in Lebanon.'

Many wounded soldiers from Operation Iron Swords experienced additional injury during the 40-day war with Iran. Security uncertainty is bringing many wounded back to a sense of threat. From Netal organization: 'Beyond the symptoms themselves, a sense of loneliness intensifies. The social circle is real oxygen for them, and when it is damaged the difficulty grows.' For some wounded, reaching a protected space is not simple and sometimes impossible.

Gilad, diagnosed with autism and serving in Iron Dome as part of integrating people with disabilities into the IDF, said: 'In a year and ten months in the army, I was surprised by the significant personal and professional support I received from the team and commanders. I was trained and learned a lot. We came to the current operation prepared, after prolonged professional preparations, and I am amazed to see every day the effort of everyone around me working nights like days and barely sleeping, for the chance to increase interception percentages, to save human lives and maintain home front security. I am proud to be part of a team of people working tirelessly so that my family and all our families can feel secure even in these days.'

'Amit's Friends Café' operates year-round as a community initiative connecting people around the memory of Amit, who fell in combat in Rafah in August 2024. The café was founded by his family and local community with the desire to continue the simple moments Amit loved most—sitting with friends, talking, laughing and being together.

Following additional Hezbollah fire, alerts sounded in Kiryat Shmona and Kfar Giladi. From Kiryat Shmona municipality: 'An alert has now been activated in Kiryat Shmona. Due to missile fire, residents are requested to enter shelters and protected spaces and remain there until receiving another notice from Home Front Command.'

Pelephone donated dozens of SIM cards and mobile devices to social workers and security personnel to enable continuous communication for those working on the aid front in the city and to strengthen the city's support line for residents seeking temporary evacuation. Yes company connected dozens of public shelters throughout the city to Yes+ service at no cost to ease prolonged shelter stays by providing diverse content for all ages.

Education Minister Yoav Kisch presented a differentiated matriculation easement framework: nationwide changes include shifting exam-to-grade-average weight to 40%-60%, allowing one internal exam instead of external in humanities subjects, and a national safety net adjusting for gaps between national and multi-year averages. Northern residents can take two internal exams in humanities subjects instead of external exams.

Northern residents warn: 'If Hezbollah is not dismantled, there will be another round.' One resident stated: 'I have no trust in the government whatsoever. They promised us quiet and security after previous rounds, and what happened? Nothing.' Another emphasized: 'The only way we will believe something real is happening is if they outlaw Hezbollah. As long as they have a political wing, schools and banks—you cannot really dismantle them.'

Due to the security situation, state Memorial Day ceremonies will be pre-recorded and broadcast via media and digital channels if live ceremonies cannot be held. Ceremonies at military cemeteries will be held subject to Home Front Command guidelines expected to be updated close to Memorial Day.

Ministry of Defense: 170 fallen soldiers added to the count in the past year; 26 soldiers fell in 'Lion's Roar' operation in northern Lebanon, including 15 killed by missile strikes and 6 in direct combat.
59,583 bereaved family members live in Israel, including 8,420 bereaved parents, 4,872 widows, 14,430 children of fallen soldiers, 31,814 siblings.

Education Minister Yoav Kish announced expanded relief measures for matriculation exams, including 40-60% weight reduction for exam grades versus protection grade, with additional accommodations for northern students.

Sderot launches pilot program to improve housing conditions by reducing 'energy poverty' — 20-30% of households pay for energy loss due to poor insulation. Professional teams conduct energy audits and develop tailored action plans.

David Azulai, head of Metula council: 'Citizens of the north feel betrayed once again... The fact that the US president announces a ceasefire shows how disconnected PM Netanyahu is from the people and the reality of northern residents.'

Asaf Langalben, head of Upper Galilee Regional Council: 'This is a pause between rounds... The north deserves a real decision that creates true security, not a temporary illusion whose end is disaster.'
Health Ministry: Kitchen at daycare facility closed after failing to meet required conditions. 15 toddlers suspected of food poisoning; 2 hospitalized at Ichilov Hospital for observation.

MDA paramedic Yosef Haim Aouzi: 'A severe incident — the child lay on the road unconscious, without pulse or breathing, with multi-system trauma after being hit by a vehicle. We immediately began resuscitation and transported him urgently to hospital in critical condition.'
5-year-old child killed by vehicle impact on Hazon Ish Street in Beit Shemesh. Transported in critical condition to Shaare Zedek Hospital where death was pronounced after resuscitation efforts.

Tens of thousands of IDF wounded are undergoing complex rehabilitation. 'Beit HaLohem' provides emotional support; 'For Success' program offers comprehensive rehabilitation including physiotherapy, climbing training, and employment pathway 'Recalculating Route' with dedicated employment department.

Thousands of families still live in old buildings without protected rooms (mamad) and sometimes only with deteriorating shelters. Urban renewal projects are stalled in committees for years while residents remain exposed to missile threats.

Survey of 329 hourly workers by 'Workers Protection' partnership: ~80% of hourly workers suffered economic harm since 'Swords of Iron' war began; only 8% reported receiving compensation covering most damage. 63% reduced basic shopping, 56% used savings, ~40% went into overdraft, ~35% sought additional work.

Education Minister Yoav Kish expanded matriculation relief measures: students can choose one humanities subject for internal exam instead of external; northern students receive additional accommodations including adapted math questions and grade bonuses.

Ministry of Defense: 170 fallen soldiers added to count since last Memorial Day; 54 disabled IDF members recognized as fallen this year. Total fallen since 1860: 25,644. Since October 7, 2023: 7,165 new bereaved family members added.
59,583 bereaved family members now live in Israel: 8,420 bereaved parents, 4,872 widows, 14,430 children of fallen soldiers, 31,814 siblings, 12 fiancées, 35 guardians.

Independence Day celebrations in the north will not take place despite ceasefire announcement. Music industry leaders stated: 'Impossible to hold a concert — technically no time to set up, and cannot rely on ceasefire. One missile and there's a disaster.'

PM Netanyahu announced to cabinet: 'Trump requested and I agreed. We remain in the security zone during the ceasefire. Where we are — we stay.' Official Israeli statement: 'No IDF plans to withdraw south of Lebanon during ceasefire.'

Barrage of fire on northern Israel: 8 casualties transported to Galilee Medical Center in Nahariya, including 2 severe (25-year-old motorcyclist with leg and head injury; 17-year-old girl with shrapnel leg injury), 1 moderate, 5 anxiety casualties.

MDA paramedic Maor Barko: 'We found a 25-year-old man on the floor, disoriented, suffering severe injuries to his body after being wounded by shrapnel from interception. We provided life-saving medical care and transported him to hospital in critical condition.'
Arad municipality beginning demolition of severely damaged buildings. 80 apartments in buildings to be demolished or fully renovated; 120 apartments so damaged residents cannot return for months.
Minutes before ceasefire took effect at midnight, Hezbollah fired heavy barrage at Nahariya and Carmiel, resulting in 8 casualties including a girl and a 'Wolt' delivery person in critical condition.

Research at Ashkelon Academic College on shelter entry during 'Lion's Roar' war: study of 121 representative sample examined prevalence and predictors of protective behavior during missile alerts. Study conducted at war's beginning.

Hotel Association launched initiative to honor reserve personnel for Independence Day 78: second night at 50% discount or third night free for those who served 30+ days in 2026. Campaign runs through Saturday; stays April 19-24.

National Insurance: 14,815 bereaved family members receiving benefits; 367 added since last Memorial Day. 2,399 bereaved parents (55 new); 1,088 widows/widowers (30 new); 4,932 orphans (142 new); 6,396 bereaved siblings (140 new).

Ministry of Defense: 25,644 fallen soldiers since 1860. 170 added in past year; 59,583 bereaved family members now live in Israel including 8,420 bereaved parents, 4,872 widows, 14,430 children of fallen, 31,814 siblings.
National Insurance: 99,156 civilians recognized as victims of hostile acts; ~49,113 recognized as disabled at various levels. 72% of all civilian casualties (71,562) live in southern Israel.

Education Minister Yoav Kish announced expanded matriculation relief: 'A reality of uncertainty and pressure has been created that is not only pedagogical but also psychological. Northern students face exceptional circumstances requiring precise response. The framework creates certainty and allows each student to approach exams calmly and fairly.'

IDF announced: Reserve service suspended for personnel recognized as disabled by Rehabilitation Department to allow time for health treatment. Inactive reservists with medical diagnosis: service frozen pending further notice. Active reservists: service continues until status resolved with medical and command personnel.

Vehicle caught fire in Kiryat Shemona after rocket impact. Three fire crews responded. Vehicle burned; light damage from shrapnel and blast to nearby buildings and three vehicles that caught fire. No casualties reported.

Moshe Davidowitz, head of Matte Asher Regional Council and ceasefire line forum chair: 'Agreements are signed in ties in Washington, but the price is paid in blood, destroyed homes, and shattered communities here... A 'ceasefire' without lethal enforcement against Hezbollah violations and clean security space to Litani is not a political achievement — it's a death sentence waiting for the next massacre.'

Heavy barrage fired at northern Israel shortly before ceasefire took effect: over 10 launches plus two unmanned aircraft. One man severely wounded in Carmiel. Alerts sounded in Carmiel, Nahariya, and surrounding communities. Reports of explosions and interceptions.

MDA announced enhanced deployment for Independence Day 78: hundreds of paramedics, paramedics, first-aid providers, ambulances, intensive care units, motorcycles, and rescue vehicles deployed nationwide. Helicopters on standby in north and south; 4x4 vehicles at coastal stations; speedboat ICU on Kinneret; sea ambulance in Eilat.

Police announced preparations for Jerusalem Marathon on Friday April 17: hundreds of officers, Border Police, volunteers, and marshals deployed along routes. Traffic diversions planned; dozens of streets closed. Vehicles parked along race routes cannot leave until event ends. Parking banned on Ben Zvi and State Comptroller streets from Thursday 4pm.

IDF spokesman: 'IDF prepared for possibility of fire from Lebanese territory targeting northern area in light of recent developments. IDF conducting ongoing situation assessments. Currently no change in Home Front Command guidelines. If change occurs, IDF will update public and authorities in orderly manner.'
Warning sirens sound in the northern border city of Kiryat Shmona and the surrounding area due to an attack from Hezbollah.

Memorial Day ceremonies will be held in accordance with Home Front Command wartime restrictions; state ceremonies will be filmed in advance and broadcast on TV and digital platforms if in-person events cannot take place.
Home Front Command wartime restrictions limit gatherings to 5,000 attendees in some areas of the north, West Bank, Jerusalem and the south; 1,000 people in central Israel and other areas.

KKL-JNF announces NIS 30 million budget to give around 15,000 northern residents living up to 9 kilometers from the border five days in hotels with half board, free transportation and activities; also budgeted NIS 800,000 to take school pupils away from border area to quieter classrooms.
KKL launched first respite program in late March, taking 6,000 people living within 2 kilometers of Lebanese border for two-night hotel rest.

Metula Mayor David Azoulay: 'residents of the north feel betrayed once again by the deal' and 'The fact that it is the president of the United States who is the one announcing a ceasefire only highlights how disconnected the prime minister of Israel is from the people, and from the reality of the residents of the north.'
Magen David Adom reports a 25-year-old man in Karmiel seriously wounded by Hezbollah rocket fragments; 10 rockets fired at Karmiel with 8 intercepted.

Magen David Adom reports three people injured by Hezbollah rocket barrages: a 25-year-old male motorcyclist and 17-year-old girl in Karmiel listed in serious condition from shrapnel; a man in his 40s in Nahariya moderately injured.
Sirens sounded minutes before ceasefire deadline as Hezbollah fired barrage of five rockets at Galilee Panhandle; most intercepted, one struck open area.
Israel has begun returning to normal after weeks of conflict, with schools reopening and air raid sirens becoming less frequent.
Many are amazed at Israel's resilience; a shaky ceasefire has offered respite after weeks of conflict.
Many have recently been complaining about mental fog, difficulty concentrating, irritability, or a decline in mood after almost three years of living in the shadow of endless wars on various fronts.

In the period after fighting, when sirens have decreased and routine begins to return, many discover their body is not in a hurry to relax; feelings of fatigue, tension and imbalance remain and sometimes intensify. The nervous system can remain in a state of alert, as if danger is still present.
A resident described weeks of sleep punctuated by sirens, working from home while caring for children, and then being told to return to the office immediately.

Behind the veneer of Israel's famed resilience, darker feelings are simmering. Parents express pessimism: 'Can we all just get a paid spa day while our kids are in school before we go back to our bomb shelters?' and 'I'm trying to do as much as I can now before the war starts up again.'
Children were sent back to school just hours after ceasefire began, after weeks of canceled classes and scattershot online learning. Cafes and beaches filled once again with Israelis.
Israelis are relieved they no longer have to plan their lives around proximity to bomb shelters, and restrictions on gatherings have been lifted. Many are embracing a return to normalcy.

Dozens of Palestinian children unable to go to school in West Bank village of Umm al-Khair because barbed wire erected by Jewish settlers from nearby Carmel settlement blocked their usual safe path through a valley.

Khalil Hathaleen, head of Umm al-Khair village council, reported Israeli soldiers fired teargas, causing several children to experience breathing difficulties; residents described children's symptoms as if they were suffocating.
A 25-year-old man was severely wounded in the upper Galilee by Hezbollah missile shrapnel, hours after ceasefire announcement
Magen David Adom reported treating people suffering from anxiety in the area
Poll findings: 'despair and pessimism as dominant sentiments, alongside high levels of fatigue and clear expectation that conflict is far from over'
Shrapnel from Hezbollah rocket strike severely wounded a 25-year-old man in Carmiel; three others treated for stress symptoms
Three people treated for stress symptoms following Hezbollah rocket barrage
'Step by Step' program operates under Belev Echad, helping 18 wounded soldiers rebuild routine and purpose through intensive physical training, supporting recovery from injury and PTSD
Wounded soldiers in program are coping with ongoing symptoms of Post-traumatic stress disorder; many arrive with no routine, no sleep, no physical baseline

Bereaved parent Goren: 'It is a very respectful and human place. There are many fallen soldiers from the war there, and my parents are there as well. It allows people to connect to the pain of what has happened here over the past three years.'
Israel Memorial Day 2026: 170 soldiers killed, 79 victims of terror since last year

Moshe Davidovich, head of Mateh Asher Regional Council: ceasefire without 'lethal enforcement against Hezbollah for any violation' and terror-free security zone 'is not a diplomatic achievement, it is a sentence of waiting for the next massacre'
A man in his mid-20s was seriously wounded near Karmiel as a result of Hezbollah strike; several people treated for acute anxiety
Several people suffering from acute anxiety following Hezbollah barrage
30 public and educational facilities damaged in Arad missile strike, including city's cultural hall and community center
Ari Spitz, severely wounded IDF soldier: 'Let's try to find as many people as possible who promote togetherness and emphasize the importance of listening to one another, and less division.'

Ari Spitz: 'Today I'm a law student. Rehabilitation is a lifelong process, and I still have a few surgeries ahead of me, and I'm combining everything.' Hopes Israel will achieve 'clear victory in what he described as a just war on all fronts.'
Israeli Ministry of Defense: 25,644 Israeli service members killed in action from 1860 to present; 170 fallen soldiers added since last Memorial Day
59,583 bereaved family members living in Israel: 8,420 bereaved parents, 4,872 widows/widowers, 14,430 orphans; 7,165 became bereaved since October 2023

Yoseph Haddad, critically wounded in 2006 battle, upon seeing IDF destruction of building where his commander fell: 'I will never forget this. Do you understand what's happening in my heart right now in terms of pride? They are settling an old score; they've closed a wound that has been open for 20 years.'
A 25-year-old man severely wounded near Karmiel by Hezbollah missile shrapnel, with severe penetrating wounds to head and leg
